title: The gift of the Holy Ghost

opening.text: Do you remember driving with a paper map? You unfolded it on the passenger seat. You tried to read it while keeping your eyes on the road. You missed a turn, and then you had to find a place to pull over, unfold the map again, and figure out where you were.

Now think of a voice that comes with the car. It knows where you are. It tells you what to do before the turn comes. When you miss one, it says calmly, "Turn around when possible." It does not get frustrated. It does not leave.

I think of the gift of the Holy Ghost a little like that. The gospel gives us a map. The scriptures and the prophets show us the road. But we are also given a guide who rides along. He is with us in real time. He knows the road ahead, and He knows us.
But He is more than a guide. He comforts us when we are scared. He teaches us what we need to know. He tells us what is true. And He is given to us as a gift.
Today I want to talk about who He is, how we receive Him, and how we can learn to hear Him.

mainMessage.text: The gift of the Holy Ghost is a gift from God. After baptism, we receive this companion who comforts, teaches, and guides us. When we learn to hear Him and keep our lives in tune, we are never walking alone.

blocks.text: Let's start with who He is. Jesus told His disciples about Him on the night before the crucifixion. They were afraid. They knew He was leaving. And He made them a promise.

And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
Another Comforter. That means Jesus was a comforter, too, and now He would send another. And notice, He says he "may abide with you for ever." Not for a visit. To abide.
Then Jesus told them what the Comforter would do.
But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
He teaches. He brings things to our remembrance. Have you ever been in a hard moment and suddenly remembered a scripture or a line from a lesson? That is what this verse is describing.
The Holy Ghost is the third member of the Godhead. He is a spirit, a personage, not a feeling or a force. He works with the Father and the Son. He testifies of Them. He is real, and He is kind.
How do we receive this gift? There is a pattern, and it is found in the scriptures.
After the people of Samaria were baptized, the apostles in Jerusalem heard about it. They sent Peter and John to help.

Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.) Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.

See the order. First baptism. Then the laying on of hands. Then, they received the Holy Ghost. The apostles did not think the baptism was enough by itself. They came to give the gift. That is why, in our Church, a person is confirmed a member and given the gift of the Holy Ghost, usually soon after baptism, by priesthood holders who lay their hands on the person's head.
The Lord confirmed this pattern in our day.
And whoso having faith you shall confirm in my church, by the laying on of the hands, and I will bestow the gift of the Holy Ghost upon them.
I will bestow. That is the Lord speaking. He is the one who gives. The priesthood holders are His hands, but the gift is His.

There is a difference between feeling the influence of the Holy Ghost and having the gift of the Holy Ghost. Anyone can feel the Spirit at times. He can touch the hearts of those who are seeking truth. But the gift is a promise of His constant companionship, as long as we stay worthy. It is a standing invitation.
Now, a question that matters a great deal. How does He speak?
Many of us expect something dramatic. A booming voice. A bright light. But the scriptures show something different. The prophet Elijah was on a mountain, waiting to hear from the Lord.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
Wind. Earthquake. Fire. And then, a still small voice. That is how the Lord often speaks. Quietly.
In our day, He explained how that voice reaches us.

Yea, behold, I will tell you in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost, which shall come upon you and which shall dwell in your heart. Now, behold, this is the spirit of revelation; behold, this is the spirit by which Moses brought the children of Israel through the Red Sea on dry ground.
In your mind and in your heart. That is where He speaks. It is not in the ears.
President Boyd K. Packer spoke about this often. In his talk "Personal Revelation: The Gift, the Test, and the Promise," from the October 1994 general conference, he said:

The Holy Ghost speaks with a voice that you feel more than you hear. It is described as a “still small voice” \[D&C 85:6\]. And while we speak of “listening” to the whisperings of the Spirit, most often one describes a spiritual prompting by saying, “I had a feeling . . .
Have you ever said, "I had a feeling"? That may be the Holy Ghost. He often comes as a feeling.
President Packer came back to this theme in his talk "Counsel to Youth," from the October 2011 general conference. He said:

The voice of the Spirit comes as a feeling rather than a sound. You will learn, as I have learned, to “listen” for that voice that is felt rather than heard. . . . The gift of the Holy Ghost, if you consent, will guide and protect you and even correct your actions. It is a spiritual voice that comes into the mind as a thought or a feeling put into your heart. . . . It is not expected that you go through life without making mistakes, but you will not make a major mistake without first being warned by the promptings of the Spirit.

There are two things I want you to hear. First, you will learn to listen. It takes practice. Second, "if you consent." The Spirit does not force Himself on us. We invite Him, and we have to be willing to listen.
So what does this guide do for us? The scriptures give a clear list.
Jesus said that the Spirit of truth would guide His disciples.

Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.
He guides us into truth. And notice, He does not speak of Himself. He points us toward the Father and the Son. A good guide does not draw attention to himself. He helps you get where you are going.
Nephi said it simply.
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
All things what ye should do. That is a sweeping promise. Not just big decisions. Daily ones. What to say to a friend who is struggling. Whether to take a job. How to help a child who is hurting.
And Moroni taught that He gives us the most important knowledge of all.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
The truth of all things. That includes the truth that Jesus is the Christ. That the Book of Mormon is true. That Heavenly Father knows you.
Elder David A. Bednar compared the Holy Ghost to something from the Book of Mormon. In his talk "That We May Always Have His Spirit to Be with Us," from the April 2006 general conference, he said:

As we strive to align our attitudes and actions with righteousness, then the Holy Ghost becomes for us today what the Liahona was for Lehi and his family in their day. The very factors that caused the Liahona to work for Lehi will likewise invite the Holy Ghost into our lives. And the very factors that caused the Liahona not to work anciently will likewise cause us to withdraw ourselves from the Holy Ghost today.
The Liahona was a compass given to Lehi's family. It worked when they were faithful. It stopped working when they were not. Elder Bednar says the Holy Ghost is like that for us.
He added a short summary in the same talk:
The Spirit of the Lord can be our guide and will bless us with direction, instruction, and spiritual protection during our mortal journey.
Direction. Instruction. Protection. If you are ever wondering what the gift is for, there is your list.
Here is a hard truth. We can lose the sound of that guide. The voice does not leave. We tune it out.
Paul warned the Ephesians about this.
And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.
Grieve not. The Spirit has feelings, in a sense. When we choose things that offend Him, He steps back. Not because He hates us. Because He cannot stay where He is not welcome.
President Henry B. Eyring named one of the biggest reasons we miss Him. In his talk "Prayer," from the October 2001 general conference, he said:
Pride creates a noise within us which makes the quiet voice of the Spirit hard to hear. And soon, in our vanity, we no longer even listen for it. We can come quickly to think we don't need it.
Pride creates noise. If the Spirit speaks quietly, then we need quiet hearts to hear.
The Lord has given us a promise about how to keep Him near. It comes in a revelation to Joseph Smith, from Liberty Jail.

Let thy bowels also be full of charity towards all men, and to the household of faith, and let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly; then shall thy confidence wax strong in the presence of God; and the doctrine of the priesthood shall distil upon thy soul as the dews from heaven. The Holy Ghost shall be thy constant companion, and thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth; and thy dominion shall be an everlasting dominion, and without compulsory means it shall flow unto thee forever and ever.
Let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly. That is the recipe. Clean thoughts. Charity toward people. And in return, the Holy Ghost becomes our constant companion.
President Eyring also showed us a way to invite Him in. In his talk "Serve with the Spirit," from the October 2010 general conference, he said:

Reading, studying, and pondering are not the same. We read words and we may get ideas. We study and we may discover patterns and connections in scripture. But when we ponder, we invite revelation by the Spirit. Pondering, to me, is the thinking and the praying I do after reading and studying in the scriptures carefully.
Ponder. Take a verse and sit with it. Ask a question. Listen. That is how revelation often begins.
How do we know that the Spirit is with us? There are signs. Paul listed them.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
Love. Joy. Peace. Patience. Kindness. Goodness. Faith. Meekness. Self-control. If you find yourself feeling those things, even in a hard moment, the Spirit may be near.
The prophet Moroni described how the Spirit fills us as we grow.

And the remission of sins bringeth meekness, and lowliness of heart; and because of meekness and lowliness of heart cometh the visitation of the Holy Ghost, which Comforter filleth with hope and perfect love, which love endureth by diligence unto prayer, until the end shall come, when all the saints shall dwell with God.
Hope and perfect love. When the Holy Ghost fills us, we feel hopeful. We feel loved. And it comes through meekness, which means being teachable. And through diligence in prayer.
That is the picture. A companion who comforts, teaches, guides, warns, and fills us with love. All because we were baptized, and we were given this gift, and we chose to keep it close.

story.title: Nephi is led by the Spirit

blocks.text: Nephi and his brothers had been sent back to Jerusalem to get the brass plates. Their first attempts had failed. Nephi went out alone at night, with no plan. He tells us what happened.

And I was led by the Spirit, not knowing beforehand the things which I should do. Nevertheless I went forth, and as I came near unto the house of Laban I beheld a man, and he had fallen to the earth before me, for he was drunken with wine.

Nephi did not have a map or a plan. He had the Spirit. He took one step at a time and let the guide lead him. That is how many of us are asked to live. Not with the whole route in view, but with a steady voice saying, here, now, this way.

application.text: Try these simple things this week.

First, pay attention to the feelings that come to you in quiet moments. When you think, "I should call my friend," or "I should not go there," take it seriously. Write it down if you can. Then act on it. The Spirit speaks more when we respond.
Second, set aside five quiet minutes each day. No phone. Read one verse and ponder it, like President Eyring taught.
Third, ask yourself what is making noise in your life. Is there something that crowds out the quiet voice? Choose one thing to turn down.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the Holy Ghost is real. I know that He is a gift from our Heavenly Father and that He speaks to our hearts. I have felt His comfort in hard times, and I have felt Him guide me when I did not know the way. I know that He will do the same for anyone who invites Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to take seriously the quiet feelings that come to you and act on them.
I invite you to set aside five quiet minutes each day to read one verse and ponder it.
I invite you to turn down one thing that crowds out the quiet voice.
blessings: You will recognize the Spirit's voice.

closingVerse.text: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.

opening.text: When I was young, my grandfather had an old radio. It sat on a shelf in his kitchen. He would turn the dial slowly, and the room would fill with static. Hiss, crackle, a half-heard voice. Then, suddenly, a clear station. Music, or a news report, as clear as if the speaker were in the room.
The station was always there. The signal was always in the air. It just took a steady hand to tune in.

The Holy Ghost is like that signal. Heavenly Father is always sending. His Spirit is always willing to speak. But we have to tune in. We have to turn the dial with care, and we have to be in a place where the signal can reach us.
Today I want to talk about the gift of the Holy Ghost. Who He is, how we receive Him, and how we learn to tune in. If you have ever wondered whether you really hear the Spirit, I hope this will help.

mainMessage.text: After baptism, we are given the gift of the Holy Ghost. He is always ready to teach, comfort, and guide us. As we keep our hearts quiet and our lives clean, we can learn to hear Him clearly.

blocks.text: Let's begin with a promise made on a sad night. Jesus was about to leave His disciples. They were afraid. And He said:

And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
Another Comforter, who abides with us forever. Jesus did not leave His disciples without help. He sent a Comforter who could be with each of them, wherever they went.
Then He told them what this Comforter would do.
But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
Teach. Remember. Those two things are what we need most when life gets loud. A teacher who sits with us. And a quiet reminder of what the Savior has said.
The Holy Ghost is a member of the Godhead, a personage of spirit. He is not an idea or a mood. He speaks for the Father and the Son, and He testifies of Them.
How do we receive this gift? The pattern is clear.
In Samaria, people believed Philip's message and were baptized. When the apostles in Jerusalem heard it, they sent Peter and John.

Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.) Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
The Samaritans were baptized, but the apostles knew something was still missing. The gift of the Holy Ghost is given by the laying on of hands, by someone holding the priesthood.
In our time, the Lord told the Saints how to do this.
And whoso having faith you shall confirm in my church, by the laying on of the hands, and I will bestow the gift of the Holy Ghost upon them.

This is why, after baptism, we have a confirmation. Priesthood holders place their hands on the person's head. One of them speaks, and says the words, "Receive the Holy Ghost." It is a sacred moment, and the Lord Himself bestows the gift.
A radio is only as good as its power source. Baptism opens the connection. The gift of the Holy Ghost is the power that flows through it.
Now, what does it sound like when He speaks? This is the question I get asked most.
Think of the prophet Elijah. He was waiting for the Lord on a mountain.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
He was not in the wind, the earthquake, or the fire. He was in the still small voice. If you were waiting for a loud broadcast, you could miss Him.
The Lord explained how this voice works in our day.

Yea, behold, I will tell you in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost, which shall come upon you and which shall dwell in your heart. Now, behold, this is the spirit of revelation; behold, this is the spirit by which Moses brought the children of Israel through the Red Sea on dry ground.
Mind and heart. A thought that comes. A feeling that settles.
President Boyd K. Packer helped many of us understand this. In his talk "Personal Revelation: The Gift, the Test, and the Promise," from the October 1994 general conference, he said:

The Holy Ghost speaks with a voice that you feel more than you hear. It is described as a “still small voice” \[D&C 85:6\]. And while we speak of “listening” to the whisperings of the Spirit, most often one describes a spiritual prompting by saying, “I had a feeling . . .
That is good news for anyone who feels they have never heard anything. What we call a feeling may be the Spirit, and we may not have recognized it.
In his talk "Counsel to Youth," from the October 2011 general conference, President Packer taught:

The voice of the Spirit comes as a feeling rather than a sound. You will learn, as I have learned, to “listen” for that voice that is felt rather than heard. . . . The gift of the Holy Ghost, if you consent, will guide and protect you and even correct your actions. It is a spiritual voice that comes into the mind as a thought or a feeling put into your heart. . . . It is not expected that you go through life without making mistakes, but you will not make a major mistake without first being warned by the promptings of the Spirit.
You will learn to listen. That is the key. Like tuning a radio, it takes patience. The first few times, you may hear mostly static. But with practice, the station gets clear.
And notice the phrase: if you consent. The Spirit will not push His way in. He waits for our permission. That is why a radio has a dial. We have to turn it.
Once the radio is tuned, what do we hear? The Savior described the work of the Spirit in several ways.
On the night before He died, He said:

Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.

Guide into all truth. That is the first job. And notice that He does not speak of Himself. He is like a good announcer who points us to the music, not to himself. His message always leads us to the Father and the Son.
Nephi taught what that guidance includes.
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
All things what ye should do. Not just the big turning points. Small ones too. What to say. Where to go. Whom to call.
And Moroni gave the promise that many people have tested.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
The truth of all things. When someone asks me how I know that Jesus is the Christ, I give them this verse. I know by the power of the Holy Ghost.
Elder David A. Bednar gave us a picture from the Book of Mormon. In his talk "That We May Always Have His Spirit to Be with Us," from the April 2006 general conference, he said:

As we strive to align our attitudes and actions with righteousness, then the Holy Ghost becomes for us today what the Liahona was for Lehi and his family in their day. The very factors that caused the Liahona to work for Lehi will likewise invite the Holy Ghost into our lives. And the very factors that caused the Liahona not to work anciently will likewise cause us to withdraw ourselves from the Holy Ghost today.

The Liahona worked by faith and diligence. When Lehi's family were careless, it stopped working. In the same way, the signal comes through when we keep our hearts and lives aligned, and it fades when we drift.
In the same talk, Elder Bednar said:
The Spirit of the Lord can be our guide and will bless us with direction, instruction, and spiritual protection during our mortal journey.
Direction. Instruction. Protection. That is what we are tuning in for.
What creates static? Paul named one cause in a single line.
And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.
Grieve not. We can offend the Spirit by what we do, say, and choose to take in. He does not shout. He just draws back.
President Henry B. Eyring pointed out the quiet danger of pride. In his talk "Prayer," from the October 2001 general conference, he said:
Pride creates a noise within us which makes the quiet voice of the Spirit hard to hear. And soon, in our vanity, we no longer even listen for it. We can come quickly to think we don't need it.
That is subtle. The noise is inside us. It is the voice that says, I know best. I do not need help. And once we think we do not need Him, we stop listening.
The Lord gave a promise to those who keep their thoughts clean. It was given to Joseph Smith in Liberty Jail, in one of the darkest times of his life.

Let thy bowels also be full of charity towards all men, and to the household of faith, and let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly; then shall thy confidence wax strong in the presence of God; and the doctrine of the priesthood shall distil upon thy soul as the dews from heaven. The Holy Ghost shall be thy constant companion, and thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth; and thy dominion shall be an everlasting dominion, and without compulsory means it shall flow unto thee forever and ever.
Virtue in our thoughts, and charity toward all. And what follows? The Holy Ghost as a constant companion. That is the clear station.
President Eyring also gave us a way to turn the dial. In his talk "Serve with the Spirit," from the October 2010 general conference, he said:

Reading, studying, and pondering are not the same. We read words and we may get ideas. We study and we may discover patterns and connections in scripture. But when we ponder, we invite revelation by the Spirit. Pondering, to me, is the thinking and the praying I do after reading and studying in the scriptures carefully.
Pondering is the dial. We slow down, ask, and listen. That is when the signal comes through.
How do we know we are hearing the right station? Paul listed the signs.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, meekness, self-control. If a message leaves you with those, you are in the right place. If it leaves you with fear, confusion, or anger, listen again.
Moroni added a beautiful description of what the Spirit does when He fills us.

And the remission of sins bringeth meekness, and lowliness of heart; and because of meekness and lowliness of heart cometh the visitation of the Holy Ghost, which Comforter filleth with hope and perfect love, which love endureth by diligence unto prayer, until the end shall come, when all the saints shall dwell with God.

Notice the pattern. Forgiveness leads to meekness. Meekness invites the Spirit. The Spirit fills us with hope and love. And it endures by diligence in prayer. This is not a one-time event. It is a daily tuning.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when the Holy Ghost guided, comforted, or warned them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Philip and the man in the chariot

blocks.text: Philip was walking on a desert road when an official from Ethiopia rode by in his chariot, reading from the prophet Isaiah. Philip heard a prompting.

Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.
Philip was listening. The prompting was simple: go near. He acted on it. He ran. And because he listened, a seeking man found a guide.
The Spirit prompted Philip, and Philip became the answer to someone else's need. That happens often. The Spirit sends us to people.

application.text: Here are a few steps for the coming week.
First, find your quiet. Set aside five minutes in the morning or at night, with no phone and no music. Ask Heavenly Father one real question. Then listen. Write down anything that comes.
Second, notice the small promptings that come during the day. A name that comes to mind. A thought to say something kind. Act on one of them. Each time we act, we learn to recognize the voice.
Third, look at what adds noise. Is there something you watch, read, or listen to that leaves you feeling cold or restless? Try turning it off for a week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the Holy Ghost is real. I know that He speaks to each of us in ways we can learn to recognize. I have felt His comfort, and I have followed His promptings. I have also learned what it feels like when I miss them. I know that the Lord is generous with this gift. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to find five quiet minutes, ask Heavenly Father one real question and listen.
I invite you to act on one small prompting during the day.
I invite you to turn off for a week something that leaves you feeling cold or restless.
blessings: You will learn to know the Spirit's voice.
You will be led to do good.

closingVerse.text: Did I not speak peace to your mind concerning the matter? What greater witness can you have than from God?

opening.text: Picture a cold night in the mountains. You have been hiking all day. Your hands are numb, your feet are wet, and the wind is picking up. Then you see it. A small cabin with smoke rising from the chimney. You push the door open, and the warmth hits you all at once.
A fire is burning. Someone has kept it going. You pull off your wet boots and sit near it. The shaking slowly stops. You feel safe.
That fire did not make the trip shorter or the mountain easier. But it changed how the night felt. You were no longer cold and alone.

The gift of the Holy Ghost is a lot like that. Life can be cold. We get tired, and sometimes we are afraid. And Heavenly Father has given us a source of warmth that stays with us. A Comforter. A Guide. A Teacher.
Today I want to talk about that gift. Who He is, how we receive Him, and how we keep the fire going.

mainMessage.text: The Holy Ghost is a gift from our Heavenly Father. He comforts us, teaches us, and guides us. If we tend our lives the way we tend a fire, He will stay with us.

blocks.text: Let's start with a night when the disciples were very afraid.
Jesus knew He was leaving them. So He did not just say, I will be back. He made a specific promise.

And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
Abide with you. Dwell with you. That is cabin language. A place you can come in from the cold. The Holy Ghost is meant to stay.
Then Jesus told them what He would do for them.
But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
He comforts. He teaches. He reminds. If you have ever had a scripture rise to mind when you needed it most, you have experienced that last one.
The Holy Ghost is the third member of the Godhead. He is a personage of spirit. He is one with the Father and the Son in purpose, and His work is to testify of Them.
How does the gift come to us? The answer is in the book of Acts.
Philip had taught in Samaria, and many believed and were baptized. The apostles heard and sent two of their own.

Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.) Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
They prayed. They laid on hands. And the gift was received. It was not given by chance. It was given through the priesthood.
In the Doctrine and Covenants, the Lord taught the same.
And whoso having faith you shall confirm in my church, by the laying on of the hands, and I will bestow the gift of the Holy Ghost upon them.

The Lord says, I will bestow. It is a gift, freely given, to anyone with faith who is confirmed. In a way, the person who lays on hands is like the one who opens the cabin door. The warmth inside is the Lord's.
We sometimes forget that this is a gift we can have all our lives. It does not run out after a day or a week. It stays, as long as we stay worthy to keep it.
Now, if the fire is warm, how do we hear the voice that comes with it?
Elijah learned something about this on a mountain. He was told to stand before the Lord.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
The wind did not have the Lord. The earthquake did not have the Lord. The fire did not have the Lord. A still small voice did.
The Lord described, in our day, how it works.

Yea, behold, I will tell you in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost, which shall come upon you and which shall dwell in your heart. Now, behold, this is the spirit of revelation; behold, this is the spirit by which Moses brought the children of Israel through the Red Sea on dry ground.
In your mind and in your heart. A quiet certainty. A warmth in the chest. A thought that is not your usual thought.
President Boyd K. Packer taught this with care. In his talk "Personal Revelation: The Gift, the Test, and the Promise," from the October 1994 general conference, he said:

The Holy Ghost speaks with a voice that you feel more than you hear. It is described as a “still small voice” \[D&C 85:6\]. And while we speak of “listening” to the whisperings of the Spirit, most often one describes a spiritual prompting by saying, “I had a feeling . . .
A feeling. The warmth of a fire is also a feeling, and no one doubts it is real.
In his talk "Counsel to Youth," from the October 2011 general conference, President Packer added:

The voice of the Spirit comes as a feeling rather than a sound. You will learn, as I have learned, to “listen” for that voice that is felt rather than heard. . . . The gift of the Holy Ghost, if you consent, will guide and protect you and even correct your actions. It is a spiritual voice that comes into the mind as a thought or a feeling put into your heart. . . . It is not expected that you go through life without making mistakes, but you will not make a major mistake without first being warned by the promptings of the Spirit.
Guide. Protect. Correct. Warn. That is quite a list. He is not only a warm fire. He is also a friend who taps your shoulder when you are about to step off the path.
And again, notice the words if you consent. The fire only warms the one who comes in and sits near it.
What does the Spirit do for us, once we are near the fire?
Jesus said it plainly.

Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.
He guides into all truth. And He does not speak of Himself. A good friend by the fire does not put on a show. He tells you what is true and helps you see what you need to see.
Nephi taught that the Spirit will show us what to do.
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
There is a condition. If ye will enter in by the way. That means baptism, and then the gift. After that, the Spirit shows us what to do.
And Moroni taught that He reveals what is true.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
I have known some people who say, "I wish I could know for sure." Moroni gives us the way. By the power of the Holy Ghost.

Elder David A. Bednar used a story from the Book of Mormon to teach how the Spirit guides. In his talk "That We May Always Have His Spirit to Be with Us," from the April 2006 general conference, he said:

As we strive to align our attitudes and actions with righteousness, then the Holy Ghost becomes for us today what the Liahona was for Lehi and his family in their day. The very factors that caused the Liahona to work for Lehi will likewise invite the Holy Ghost into our lives. And the very factors that caused the Liahona not to work anciently will likewise cause us to withdraw ourselves from the Holy Ghost today.
A compass works only if you are willing to follow the direction it gives. And the Liahona stopped working for Lehi's family when they stopped trusting.
He summed it up in this line:
The Spirit of the Lord can be our guide and will bless us with direction, instruction, and spiritual protection during our mortal journey.
In a cold place, those three gifts mean a lot. Direction when we are lost. Instruction when we are unsure. Protection when we are in danger.
A fire needs tending. If we ignore it, it goes out. What puts out the fire of the Spirit?
Paul had a short and serious warning.
And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.
Grieve not. A fire can be smothered. And the Spirit can be pushed away by anger, cruelty, and sin.
President Henry B. Eyring spoke about one thing that does this very quietly. In his talk "Prayer," from the October 2001 general conference, he said:
Pride creates a noise within us which makes the quiet voice of the Spirit hard to hear. And soon, in our vanity, we no longer even listen for it. We can come quickly to think we don't need it.
Pride. It does not feel like danger. It feels like confidence. But it can lead us away from the fire without our noticing.
So how do we keep the fire burning? The Lord gave Joseph Smith a promise from Liberty Jail.

Let thy bowels also be full of charity towards all men, and to the household of faith, and let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly; then shall thy confidence wax strong in the presence of God; and the doctrine of the priesthood shall distil upon thy soul as the dews from heaven. The Holy Ghost shall be thy constant companion, and thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth; and thy dominion shall be an everlasting dominion, and without compulsory means it shall flow unto thee forever and ever.
Charity toward all. Virtue in our thoughts. Those are the logs we put on the fire. And the promise is that the Holy Ghost will be our constant companion.
President Eyring taught a practice that keeps the fire going. In his talk "Serve with the Spirit," from the October 2010 general conference, he said:

Reading, studying, and pondering are not the same. We read words and we may get ideas. We study and we may discover patterns and connections in scripture. But when we ponder, we invite revelation by the Spirit. Pondering, to me, is the thinking and the praying I do after reading and studying in the scriptures carefully.
Ponder. Think. Pray. That is a way of leaning in toward the fire. And the Spirit meets us there.
How do we know if we are feeling the right warmth? Paul named the fruit.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
Love. Joy. Peace. That is what the Spirit leaves behind. If you leave a quiet moment of prayer feeling love and peace, you were by the fire.
Moroni described something deeper.

And the remission of sins bringeth meekness, and lowliness of heart; and because of meekness and lowliness of heart cometh the visitation of the Holy Ghost, which Comforter filleth with hope and perfect love, which love endureth by diligence unto prayer, until the end shall come, when all the saints shall dwell with God.
Lowliness of heart. That means being humble and teachable. And the result: a Comforter who fills us with hope and perfect love.
That is the warmth we want. And it lasts, Moroni says, when we are diligent in prayer. The fire burns for those who keep tending it.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when the Holy Ghost guided, comforted, or warned them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Peter and the three men

blocks.text: Peter was on a rooftop in Joppa, thinking about a strange vision he had just seen. At that same moment, three men were at the door, sent by a Roman officer named Cornelius. Peter did not know that. But the Spirit did.
While Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit said unto him, Behold, three men seek thee. Arise therefore, and get thee down, and go with them, doubting nothing: for I have sent them.

Peter was thinking, pondering. And the Spirit spoke. Peter had been taught that he should not go to the home of a Gentile. But when the Spirit said, go with them, doubting nothing, he went. And that obedience opened the gospel to the Gentiles.
The Spirit knew what Peter did not. That is the gift of a guide who sees the whole road.

application.text: Here are a few things to try this week.
First, tend the fire. Pick one daily habit that invites the Spirit. It might be reading a short passage of scripture and pondering it. It might be praying before you start your day.
Second, watch for the fruit. At the end of each day, ask yourself, "When did I feel love, peace, or joy today?" That is often the Spirit.
Third, remove one thing that smothers the fire. Maybe it is a habit, a show, or a way of talking about people. Replace it with something that makes you feel closer to Heavenly Father.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the Holy Ghost is a gift from a loving Heavenly Father. I know that He comforts, teaches, and guides. I have felt His warmth on cold days, and I have felt Him lead me when I did not know the way. I know that this gift is for everyone who is baptized and confirmed. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

I invite you to ask each night, "When did I feel love, peace or joy today?"
I invite you to remove one thing that smothers the fire.
blessings: The Spirit will be with you more.
You will see the fruit of the Spirit.
You will feel closer to Heavenly Father.

closingVerse.text: And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

opening.text: Imagine someone gives you a gift. It is wrapped in nice paper, tied with a ribbon. You say thank you, and you set it on a shelf. A week goes by. A month. A year. You walk past it every day, but you never open it.
What would that say about the gift? Nothing. It would still be a good gift. But it would not do anything for you. The value is inside the box, and the box is closed.

The gift of the Holy Ghost can be like that. Every baptized member of the Church has been given it. Hands were laid on our heads. We were told, "Receive the Holy Ghost." And then for many of us, life went on. We did not think much about it again.
But this gift is not meant to sit on a shelf. It is meant to be opened, used, and enjoyed every day.
Today I want to talk about how to open it. I will speak about who the Holy Ghost is, how we received Him, how He speaks, and how we can use this gift more fully.

mainMessage.text: The gift of the Holy Ghost is given to every member at confirmation. It becomes a living blessing when we open it, listen to it, and live in a way that welcomes the Spirit.

blocks.text: Before we open a gift, it helps to know who gave it and what is inside.
The Giver is our Heavenly Father, who sends the Holy Ghost in the name of His Son. Jesus described what we would find in the box.

And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
A Comforter. The Spirit of truth. One who abides, one who dwells with us. Those are not small things.
Jesus gave more detail about what He would do.
But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.

Inside the box, there is a Teacher and a Helper to remember. Many people feel they have forgotten things they once learned. This promise says the Holy Ghost can bring back what we need, when we need it.
The Holy Ghost is a member of the Godhead. He is a personage of spirit. He is not a force or a feeling alone. He is a living person who loves us and wants to help.
How was the gift wrapped and delivered? By the laying on of hands.
The New Testament shows this in the city of Samaria. Many had been baptized. But something was still missing.

Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.) Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
The gift was given by the laying on of hands. It was a second step after baptism. And the apostles were careful to do it.
In our day, the Lord again described how to do it.
And whoso having faith you shall confirm in my church, by the laying on of the hands, and I will bestow the gift of the Holy Ghost upon them.
I will bestow. Heavenly Father is the Giver. Priesthood holders are His hands. And the one who receives is blessed with a companion who can remain with them.
There is a very important line to remember. The gift is given, but it is kept by the way we live. It is ours as long as we stay worthy. That is what makes it a gift we have to open and use.
So how does the gift speak when we open it? The scriptures give a surprising answer.
The prophet Elijah stood on a mountain, waiting for the Lord.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
The Lord was not in the wind. Not in the earthquake. Not in the fire. In a still small voice. Quiet. Easy to miss.
The Lord explained how this works in modern revelation.

Yea, behold, I will tell you in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost, which shall come upon you and which shall dwell in your heart. Now, behold, this is the spirit of revelation; behold, this is the spirit by which Moses brought the children of Israel through the Red Sea on dry ground.
He speaks in the mind and the heart. A thought. A feeling.
President Boyd K. Packer explained this in his talk "Personal Revelation: The Gift, the Test, and the Promise," from the October 1994 general conference:

The Holy Ghost speaks with a voice that you feel more than you hear. It is described as a “still small voice” \[D&C 85:6\]. And while we speak of “listening” to the whisperings of the Spirit, most often one describes a spiritual prompting by saying, “I had a feeling . . .
A feeling more than a sound. If we are waiting for a voice in the ear, we may miss the gift that is already working.
In his talk "Counsel to Youth," from the October 2011 general conference, he said:

The voice of the Spirit comes as a feeling rather than a sound. You will learn, as I have learned, to “listen” for that voice that is felt rather than heard. . . . The gift of the Holy Ghost, if you consent, will guide and protect you and even correct your actions. It is a spiritual voice that comes into the mind as a thought or a feeling put into your heart. . . . It is not expected that you go through life without making mistakes, but you will not make a major mistake without first being warned by the promptings of the Spirit.
Notice that this gift does three things. It guides, protects, and corrects. And it warns us before we make a major mistake. That is a gift that is worth opening.
Now, what is inside the box? Let's open it and look.
Jesus said the first thing is truth.

Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.
He guides into all truth. And He does not talk about Himself. He is like a gift that points you to the One who gave it.
The second thing is direction for daily life. Nephi taught:
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
All things what ye should do. That is a gift for a busy person. We make dozens of choices every day. This gift offers help.
The third thing is a witness of truth.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
The truth of all things. When people ask how we know the Book of Mormon is true, or that Jesus is the Christ, we point to this gift.
Elder David A. Bednar described it with a picture from the Book of Mormon. In his talk "That We May Always Have His Spirit to Be with Us," from the April 2006 general conference, he said:

As we strive to align our attitudes and actions with righteousness, then the Holy Ghost becomes for us today what the Liahona was for Lehi and his family in their day. The very factors that caused the Liahona to work for Lehi will likewise invite the Holy Ghost into our lives. And the very factors that caused the Liahona not to work anciently will likewise cause us to withdraw ourselves from the Holy Ghost today.
The Liahona was a gift, too. It came to Lehi's family on the ground outside their tent. But it only worked for those who followed it with faith. Gifts need us to use them.
He gave a short summary:
The Spirit of the Lord can be our guide and will bless us with direction, instruction, and spiritual protection during our mortal journey.
Direction, instruction, and protection. When you open the box, that is what you find.
A gift can be damaged. How do we keep this one safe?
Paul gave a warning that fits here.
And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.
Grieve not. We can hurt this gift. We can set it down and walk away. Through unkind words, through anger, through habits we know are wrong.
President Henry B. Eyring warned us about one cause. In his talk "Prayer," from the October 2001 general conference, he said:
Pride creates a noise within us which makes the quiet voice of the Spirit hard to hear. And soon, in our vanity, we no longer even listen for it. We can come quickly to think we don't need it.
Pride is the dust that settles on a gift left on the shelf. It starts to feel like we do not need it. And then, little by little, we stop reaching for it.
The Lord gave us the way to keep the gift bright. It was given to the Prophet Joseph Smith while he was in a cold jail cell.

Let thy bowels also be full of charity towards all men, and to the household of faith, and let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly; then shall thy confidence wax strong in the presence of God; and the doctrine of the priesthood shall distil upon thy soul as the dews from heaven. The Holy Ghost shall be thy constant companion, and thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth; and thy dominion shall be an everlasting dominion, and without compulsory means it shall flow unto thee forever and ever.
Charity. Virtue. Those are how we polish the gift. And the promise is that the Holy Ghost will be a constant companion.
President Eyring also taught a daily way to use it. In his talk "Serve with the Spirit," from the October 2010 general conference, he said:

Reading, studying, and pondering are not the same. We read words and we may get ideas. We study and we may discover patterns and connections in scripture. But when we ponder, we invite revelation by the Spirit. Pondering, to me, is the thinking and the praying I do after reading and studying in the scriptures carefully.
Pondering is how we open the box a little further each day.
What does it look like when the gift is in use? Paul described the results.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, meekness, self-control. A person living with this gift will gradually look and sound different. Not perfect. But softer. Stronger. Kinder.
Moroni added one more description.

And the remission of sins bringeth meekness, and lowliness of heart; and because of meekness and lowliness of heart cometh the visitation of the Holy Ghost, which Comforter filleth with hope and perfect love, which love endureth by diligence unto prayer, until the end shall come, when all the saints shall dwell with God.
Hope and perfect love. When the gift is in use, hope grows. Fear shrinks. Love expands.
And Moroni says that it endures by diligence unto prayer. A gift that is used often becomes a part of us.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when the Holy Ghost guided, comforted, or warned them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The day of Pentecost

blocks.text: After Jesus ascended, His disciples waited together in Jerusalem. They had been told to wait for power from on high. On the day of Pentecost, it came.

And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

Notice the setting. They were all with one accord, in one place. They were together, and they were ready. Then the gift came, and it filled them. Frightened disciples became bold witnesses. This is what the gift can do for a person who receives it with faith.

application.text: Here are some ideas to try this week.
Open the gift. Take a moment tonight to say a short prayer. Thank Heavenly Father for the gift of the Holy Ghost, and ask Him to help you recognize it.
Use the gift. Before a decision, big or small, stop and ask for help. Then listen for how you feel.
Protect the gift. Pick one thing that drives the Spirit away from your home or your mind. It might be a habit of arguing, or a kind of media. Replace it with something that invites the Spirit.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the gift of the Holy Ghost is real. I know that Heavenly Father gave it because He loves us. I have opened this gift at times, and I have felt His help. I have also left it on the shelf, and I know the difference. I know that He is always ready. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to thank Heavenly Father for the gift of the Holy Ghost tonight.
I invite you to stop and ask for help before a decision, big or small.
I invite you to replace one thing that drives the Spirit away with something that invites Him.
blessings: Your home will feel more peaceful.

closingVerse.text: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.

opening.text: Imagine driving across the country, alone. Long hours. Dark roads. You have the radio on, but after a while it gets old. You catch yourself nodding off. You are not sure of the next turn. You wish someone were beside you.

Now picture the same drive with a good friend in the passenger seat. They watch the road signs. They notice when you are tired. They say, "I think that was our exit." They talk with you, and the miles go by easily. Even when something goes wrong, you are not alone in it.

The gift of the Holy Ghost is a companion like that. Not just for road trips. For life. He sits beside us. He sees what we cannot see. He speaks up when we are about to make a wrong turn. And He keeps us company when we are tired and afraid.
Today I want to talk about that Companion. Who He is, how we received Him, how we recognize His voice, and how we keep Him in the seat beside us.

mainMessage.text: The Holy Ghost is a constant companion given to us after baptism. If we welcome Him, listen to Him, and live in a way that keeps Him near, He will comfort, teach, and guide us through all of life.

blocks.text: Let's begin at the Last Supper. Jesus told His disciples He would soon leave them. They were worried. So He gave a promise.

And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
Another Comforter. He said he would abide with them. That means He would stay. That is what a companion does.
Then Jesus told them what the Companion would do.
But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
He teaches all things. He brings things back to our memory. He does what a good friend does when they say, "Remember what you told me last week?"
The Holy Ghost is the third member of the Godhead. He is a personage of spirit. He is not a feeling that comes and goes. He is a real being who works in unity with the Father and the Son.
How is this Companion given to us? The Lord set a pattern, and it shows up in the New Testament.
The new believers in Samaria had been baptized. Then the apostles heard, and they sent help.

Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.) Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
The pattern is two steps. Baptism, then the laying on of hands. Both were needed.
The Lord gave the same instruction in our day.
And whoso having faith you shall confirm in my church, by the laying on of the hands, and I will bestow the gift of the Holy Ghost upon them.
I will bestow. It is the Lord who gives. The priesthood holders place their hands on the head, and the Lord gives the gift.

There is a difference between a visit and a companion. Anyone can feel the Spirit at times, especially when they are searching for truth. But the gift of the Holy Ghost is the right to have the Spirit with us continually, if we are worthy. It is a standing seat in the car.
How does the Companion talk to us? It may not sound like what you expect.
Elijah was waiting for the Lord on a mountain. He had been through a hard time and needed an answer.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
Not the wind, not the earthquake, not the fire. The Lord came in a still small voice. A good passenger does not shout. He speaks quietly and trusts you to listen.
In our own time, the Lord explained.

Yea, behold, I will tell you in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost, which shall come upon you and which shall dwell in your heart. Now, behold, this is the spirit of revelation; behold, this is the spirit by which Moses brought the children of Israel through the Red Sea on dry ground.
In your mind. In your heart. Those are the places where He talks.
President Boyd K. Packer said it simply. In his talk "Personal Revelation: The Gift, the Test, and the Promise," from the October 1994 general conference, he said:

The Holy Ghost speaks with a voice that you feel more than you hear. It is described as a “still small voice” \[D&C 85:6\]. And while we speak of “listening” to the whisperings of the Spirit, most often one describes a spiritual prompting by saying, “I had a feeling . . .
When you say, "I had a feeling," you may be describing your Companion.
In his talk "Counsel to Youth," from the October 2011 general conference, President Packer said:

The voice of the Spirit comes as a feeling rather than a sound. You will learn, as I have learned, to “listen” for that voice that is felt rather than heard. . . . The gift of the Holy Ghost, if you consent, will guide and protect you and even correct your actions. It is a spiritual voice that comes into the mind as a thought or a feeling put into your heart. . . . It is not expected that you go through life without making mistakes, but you will not make a major mistake without first being warned by the promptings of the Spirit.
That is the friend who says, "I think you should slow down." Not a loud voice. Not a lecture. A quiet word. And the words, if you consent, matter. We choose to listen.
What does the Companion do on the journey? Jesus listed His work.

Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.
Guide you into all truth. That means He knows the road and where it leads. He does not draw attention to Himself. He points to the Father and the Son.
Nephi told us how far that guidance reaches.
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
All things what ye should do. Think of a friend who knows you well and who also knows the way. That is who is sitting next to us.
And Moroni taught that this friend helps us know what is true.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
The truth of all things. It is how we know that Jesus is the Christ. It is how we know that a prophet has spoken for God.
Elder David A. Bednar offered a picture from the Book of Mormon. In his talk "That We May Always Have His Spirit to Be with Us," from the April 2006 general conference, he said:

As we strive to align our attitudes and actions with righteousness, then the Holy Ghost becomes for us today what the Liahona was for Lehi and his family in their day. The very factors that caused the Liahona to work for Lehi will likewise invite the Holy Ghost into our lives. And the very factors that caused the Liahona not to work anciently will likewise cause us to withdraw ourselves from the Holy Ghost today.
A companion is only helpful when we are willing to follow what they say. The Liahona worked when Lehi's family did their part.
He added this:
The Spirit of the Lord can be our guide and will bless us with direction, instruction, and spiritual protection during our mortal journey.
Direction, instruction, and protection. That is a good friend to have in the car.
A companion can be driven away. We should talk about that.
Paul warned the Saints in Ephesus.
And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.
Grieve not. We can hurt the Spirit by what we do and say. When we make choices He cannot be part of, He steps back, like a friend who gets out of the car because of how the conversation is going.
President Henry B. Eyring explained one reason we lose Him. In his talk "Prayer," from the October 2001 general conference, he said:
Pride creates a noise within us which makes the quiet voice of the Spirit hard to hear. And soon, in our vanity, we no longer even listen for it. We can come quickly to think we don't need it.
Pride turns up the volume inside us. Then the quiet voice is lost.
The Lord gave a promise to those who keep a clean heart and a charitable spirit. He gave it to Joseph Smith in Liberty Jail, in a time of deep trouble.

Let thy bowels also be full of charity towards all men, and to the household of faith, and let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly; then shall thy confidence wax strong in the presence of God; and the doctrine of the priesthood shall distil upon thy soul as the dews from heaven. The Holy Ghost shall be thy constant companion, and thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth; and thy dominion shall be an everlasting dominion, and without compulsory means it shall flow unto thee forever and ever.
Constant companion. That is the phrase for today. And the way to receive it is charity toward all, and virtue in our thoughts, without pause.
President Eyring also gave us a way to invite the Spirit to speak. In his talk "Serve with the Spirit," from the October 2010 general conference, he said:

Reading, studying, and pondering are not the same. We read words and we may get ideas. We study and we may discover patterns and connections in scripture. But when we ponder, we invite revelation by the Spirit. Pondering, to me, is the thinking and the praying I do after reading and studying in the scriptures carefully.
Ponder. It is like turning to your friend and saying, "What do you think?" Then waiting for the answer.
How do you know your friend is in the car? Paul gave us signs.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
Love, joy, peace, patience, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, self-control. When these show up in us, the Spirit is working.
Moroni described how the Spirit fills us.

And the remission of sins bringeth meekness, and lowliness of heart; and because of meekness and lowliness of heart cometh the visitation of the Holy Ghost, which Comforter filleth with hope and perfect love, which love endureth by diligence unto prayer, until the end shall come, when all the saints shall dwell with God.

A Comforter who fills us with hope and perfect love. That is what a long drive needs. And the love lasts when we are diligent in prayer. We keep talking with our Companion. We do not go silent for weeks.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when the Holy Ghost guided, comforted, or warned them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The people hear a small voice

blocks.text: After the great destruction in the Americas, a crowd gathered around the temple in the land of Bountiful. They heard a voice, and they did not know what it was.

And it came to pass that while they were thus conversing one with another, they heard a voice as if it came out of heaven; and they cast their eyes round about, for they understood not the voice which they heard; and it was not a harsh voice, neither was it a loud voice; nevertheless, and notwithstanding it being a small voice it did pierce them that did hear to the center, insomuch that there was no part of their frame that it did not cause to quake; yea, it did pierce them to the very soul, and did cause their hearts to burn. And it came to pass that again they heard the voice, and they understood it not. And again the third time they did hear the voice, and did open their ears to hear it; and their eyes were towards the sound thereof; and they did look steadfastly towards heaven, from whence the sound came.

The voice was not harsh or loud. It was small. And yet it pierced them to the very soul. They did not understand it at first, or the second time. By the third time, they opened their ears and looked toward heaven. Many of us are like them. We may need to hear it more than once before we open our ears. The Lord is patient. He speaks again.

application.text: Try these things this week.
Talk to your Companion. Each morning, say a short prayer: "Heavenly Father, please let Thy Spirit be with me today." Then pay attention.
Write down one impression. Maybe a name that came to mind. Maybe a feeling that you should do or not do something. Note it. Then act on it, if it is good. Over time, you will see the pattern.
Look at what drives Him away. If your home or your phone is full of noise, find a quiet pocket in the day. Keep it free of screens. See what you notice.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the Holy Ghost is a constant companion for those who seek Him. I know that He comforts, teaches, warns, and guides. I have been grateful for His help many times. I know that He loves us and that He is always near. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
